paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of this one, friend. Ezra gets the news and he doesn't make excuses, he doesn't point at the leaders, and he doesn't say "well, technically." He kneels and says he is ashamed and embarrassed to lift his face to God (Ezra 9:6). And notice he says "we" and "our," even though he's not the one who did it. I think that's a man who knows sin is bigger than one person's slip.

Now look at what he does in the middle of that shame. He doesn't hide from God, he runs to Him. He says that "for a brief moment, grace has come from the LORD our God," and that God "has not forsaken us in our bondage" (Ezra 9:8-9). Honest confession and big hope sit in the same prayer. That's what a good batch looks like, friend: nothing burnt covered up, and nothing thrown out either.

Then he ends where every one of us has to end. "O LORD, God of Israel, You are righteous!" and "no one can stand before You" (Ezra 9:15). Ezra doesn't bargain, he just stands there in the truth. So when you've messed up, baker, don't dodge and don't spiral. Tell God the whole truth, remember the grace He has already given, and let His commands be what you hold on to. And hang on, because this story isn't over.
